en: So we got these slash commands.
/doc, for example, could be used to generate
comments, documentation for the selected
code. But
/tests is
another interesting command which I wanna
explore here now
because
as you can also see here, you can use this
command to generate unit tests for the
selected code. And it turns out that AI is
really good when it comes to generating unit
tests.
Now if I
run
/tests here,
I could again add more information if I were
looking for specific kinds of tests or if I
only wanted to test something very specific.
But you can also just run it like this and
let the AI figure out which tests to write.
And what's really convenient here
is that it will then
go ahead
and show you which tests it wants to
generate here.
And you see,
these are the unit tests it would suggest
for this specific function.
And we could now accept this
and it did actually
add them in a new file,
a new file which I now have to save in the
project.
Like dbBackupTest, for example.
So it's also smart enough to understand that
I
probably don't want to add the unit tests in
the same file as my main application code,
but that I instead wanna have them in a
separate file like this.
And that's therefore another pretty useful
feature because writing tests
is important, but can be annoying.
Some developers absolutely don't wanna do
it. And it turns out that AI is pretty good
at that task because of course it got the
application code as very useful context.
And therefore in many cases, it's able to
figure out and write decent tests so that
you have all the tests without going through
the effort of writing them manually.
